items.text: Old House, Cross Street
The smog in the garden feels unusually dense. It has taken on an almost milky, gelatinous quality.
The damp, fishy air sticks to the visitors. Sparse ivy winds around the ancient stone wall, its bare roots clinging desperately to it.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: This right here, Miss, is the Fog Lady's house! As you can tell, it is a very big, big house, not like mine. Mine is small, but very high up!

items.speaker: Tooth Fairy
items.text: Steep, tilted roofs, sash windows, it's very Victorian.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: Hmm?

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: Oh, no, her name ain't Victoria, Miss. At least, I don't think so.

items.speaker: Tooth Fairy
items.text: No, no. I mean Victorian architecture is a kind of style of house. I'm saying this house must have a long history.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: Oh. Too right about that, Miss. It's been here for ages!

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: Come along then. I'll take you in.
Flutterpage doesn't knock, nor does she touch anything resembling a doorbell. She simply leads Tooth Fairy straight to the garden gate.

items.speaker: Vines Carbuncle
items.text: Squeak! Squeak!
Several Carbuncles peek out from among the vines before quickly retreating, their eyes still locked on the visitors.

items.speaker: Tooth Fairy
items.text: Ah! Are these her critters?

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: You lot are hungry today, ain't you?
From the folds of her oversized frock, Flutterpage pulls out a jar filled with snails.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: They ain't for you! They're for the lady of the house. Now please let me and Ms. Witch Doctor through.

items.speaker: Vines Carbuncle
items.text: Squeak!
The Carbuncles refuse their entry, shooting out a few tendrils to form a blockade.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: Sorry, Ms. Witch Doctor, they was much friendlier before.

items.speaker: Tooth Fairy
items.text: You've been here before?

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: Yep, they always let me in straight away. No clue what set them off this time.
Flutterpage stands on her tiptoes, planning to hop over the barrier, but after a quick glance at Tooth Fairy, she abandons the idea.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: I don't rightly know what to do.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: I'd try callin' her, but it won't do much good. Even if she heard me, she won't come out.

items.speaker: Tooth Fairy
items.text: You're saying she never leaves her house?

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: Not that I ever seen.

items.speaker: Tooth Fairy
items.text: Do other people visit her?

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: Hmm ... No.

items.speaker: Tooth Fairy
items.text: But you visit her often?

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: She likes when I bring her snails. You think she eats them?

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: All I know is I gave her snails, and then she asked me to stay round her house for a while.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: When she's not in a sour mood, she even teaches me some words, for arcane skills. But if she is sour, then all she does is hand me some books, and I can't even read most of them.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: Don't go askin' her too many "whys." If you do, she says "get out," and you got to go.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: So far, the longest I stayed was a whole afternoon!

items.speaker: Tooth Fairy
items.text: I see.
Tooth Fairy surveys the old mansion. To her, it looks more like a small castle than a house. She decides not to disturb the formidable witch dwelling within it.

items.speaker: Tooth Fairy
items.text: Maybe I'm the reason they aren't letting you in. I'll just stay back here.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: Alright then. Stay there, and I'll tell her about you, Miss.
The Carbuncles lower their guard as Tooth Fairy retreats. The strange plants and critters in the garden clear the way for Flutterpage as she makes her way down the path.
Flutterpage raises the snail jar high above her head, as if presenting some kind of token.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: Miss!

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: Do you hear me? Wakey-wakey!
*creak*
The lock clatters heavily, and the hinges on the old oak door give a mournful groan.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: Hmm.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: Here you go, Miss, a fresh batch of snails!
She doesn't respond. The witch's stare is fixed on the unfamiliar woman by the garden entrance.

items.speaker: Fog Hag
items.text: Who is this?

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: Hmm, well, I don't know her name, but she's a witch doctor.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: She came here in a car, with a flyer of the Uluru Qualifiers. So I think she's here for the Ulu—

items.speaker: Fog Hag
items.text: Mm?

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: Oh, I forgot that you don't like the word.

items.speaker: Tooth Fairy
items.text: Hello, Miss. I'm here investigating the source of the black fog. You can call me Tooth Fairy.

items.speaker: Fog Hag
items.text: Go away.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: But why? I ain't ask too many "whys," Miss, did I? That was only my first one today.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: Oh.
She realizes something.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: So, I can't come in at all? You promised you'd help me practice my arcane skill.

items.speaker: Fog Hag
items.text: Then you better not let me catch you saying "Uluru" ever again!
The witch anxiously snatches the snail jar from the girl's hand and closes the door.
*slam*
The door closes.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: Awh ...

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: Oh, she left me a book. Look, it's got a Carbuncle on it.

items.speaker: Tooth Fairy
items.text: Come here, Flutterpage. Are you alright?

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: I thought I could play at her house today.

items.speaker: Tooth Fairy
items.text: Would you like to do something else?

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: Like what?

items.speaker: Tooth Fairy
items.text: Like, see your new friend, Mr. Hat?

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: Mr. Hat?
LACC

items.speaker: Brimley
items.text: Ms. Flutterpage, I'll ask you to not wear me on your head.

items.speaker: Brimley
items.text: I know I can fly, but that doesn't mean you can treat me like a kite. Besides, I'm due to begin my patrol. I need to—

items.speaker: Brimley
items.text: WHOAAA!
A gust of wind blows Brimley into the hallway, spurring Flutterpage to give chase.

items.speaker: Mr. Fog
items.text: That gives us some time for business. First of all, allow me to express my respect for your adventurous spirit.

items.speaker: Mr. Fog
items.text: A haunted hag mansion whose owner feeds on snails? To visit her so quickly on your own initiative was a bold move, Ms. Tooth Fairy!
He now has no choice but to admit the existence of the witch.

items.speaker: Mr. Fog
items.text: Here's your tea. No sugar, just as you asked.
And, of course, he has kept the promised Indian tea at the forefront of his mind.

items.speaker: Tooth Fairy
items.text: The connection between this lady and the black fog will require further confirmation. However, judging from our encounter, she doesn't seem to have much concern for the world outside her home.

items.speaker: Tooth Fairy
items.text: I also noted that the word "Uluru" seemed to irritate her.

items.speaker: Mr. Fog
items.text: Uluru? As in the Uluru Games? Not a fan, I take it.

items.speaker: Mr. Fog
items.text: It's certainly odd for an arcanist to have a negative impression of the Games, though not unprecedented.

items.speaker: Mr. Fog
items.text: Which reminds me of this letter. I suspect our Fog Lady might be glad to hear it.
Mr. Fog places a voiced letter between the two of them. The paper swiftly transforms into a wide mouth.

items.speaker: Voiced Letter
items.text: "Letter from the St. Pavlov Foundation Uluru Games Organizing Committee to the Uluru London Qualifiers Organizing Committee."

items.speaker: Voiced Letter
items.text: " ... copied to the Office of the London Atmospheric Clean-up Committee ..."

items.speaker: Voiced Letter
items.text: "Due to the rapid deterioration of air quality in London and the presence of an unidentified arcane-related tuberculosis outbreak ..."

items.speaker: Voiced Letter
items.text: " ... we regretfully have decided that the Uluru London Qualifiers will be canceled until further notice to protect the health of competitors and spectators."

items.speaker: Voiced Letter
items.text: "Competitors still wishing to participate are encouraged to register for the qualifiers in Paris or other cities."
The paper folds itself up and drops back onto the table. Mr. Fog sighs.

items.speaker: Mr. Fog
items.text: I received this shortly after submitting my report concerning the events on Cross Street.

items.speaker: Tooth Fairy
items.text: They're right. It's better for everyone's health.

items.speaker: Mr. Fog
items.text: No objections here, but it's certain to cause a stir!

items.speaker: Mr. Fog
items.text: Ms. Tooth Fairy, you saw how passionate the citizens were about this event, what it means to them. They'll eat us alive when we announce this.

items.speaker: Mr. Fog
items.text: So much more so that it's canceled because of air quality. The Firm will not be pleased, I can assure you.

items.speaker: Mr. Fog
items.text: This great city will be the laughingstock of Europe, if not the entire world!

items.speaker: Mr. Fog
items.text: Unless ... Unless there's a way to clean the air in London. Perhaps then I might convince the Foundation to reconsider.

items.speaker: Tooth Fairy
items.text: Mr. Fog, there's only three weeks left before the qualifiers.

items.speaker: Tooth Fairy
items.text: It's a serious effort just to address the smog over London, let alone this new black fog and the disease that has come with it.

items.speaker: Mr. Fog
items.text: Three weeks. One for making plans, one for enacting said plans, and still one more for the final procedures.
He slumps into his chair with his arms crossed and glares furiously at the voiced letter on the desk.

items.speaker: Tooth Fairy
items.text: What are you doing now, Mr. Fog?

items.speaker: Mr. Fog
items.text: Thinking, Ms. Tooth Fairy, is how I make the plans.
Brimley, fleeing pursuit, eventually finds his way back.

items.speaker: Brimley
items.text: Forgive me for interrupting, Arthur, but I had to call off my patrol earlier than expected. I'm afraid I need a favor of you, Ms. Tooth Fairy.

items.speaker: Tooth Fairy
items.text: Hmm?

items.speaker: Brimley
items.text: Would you mind helping us with some of the sick?

items.speaker: Brimley
items.text: After that black fog rolled through, patients with this "tuber-coal-sis" variant seem to be multiplying as fast as hares in the Great Artesian Basin!
